column2: What is the friction angle δ<sub>k</sub> for a footing cast in situ?
the peak φ′<sub>k</sub>
0 – only the cohesion counts

For a footing cast in situ δ = φ′<sub>cv;k</sub>, for a smooth (precast) footing two thirds of it. The critical state angle is used because sliding involves large displacements and post-peak behaviour.
What is the partial factor γ<sub>R;h</sub> in design approach DA-2*?
For sliding γ<sub>R;h</sub> = 1.1 (for bearing resistance γ<sub>R;v</sub> = 1.4).
In the undrained case, what is the upper limit of the shear resistance?
A<sub>c</sub> · c<sub>u;k</sub>, without a limit
there is no limit

Water or air may get between the footing and the soil, so R<sub>d</sub> ≤ 0.4·V<sub>d</sub>. It may only be omitted if suction prevents a gap from forming even where there is no positive contact pressure – this is rare.
Why can usually only one half to two thirds of the passive earth resistance be taken into account?
because the soil strength is lower than expected
because the full passive resistance needs a significant displacement
because EC7 forbids the full value
because groundwater always reduces it

The passive resistance is only fully mobilised after significant compression; at the allowable displacement only part of it develops. In addition, erosion, later excavation or shrinkage of the clay may remove it altogether.
Which variable load may be included in V′<sub>k</sub>?
only one that surely acts together with H<sub>d</sub>
only the wind load
traffic on the backfill, always
The vertical force increases the resistance, so only a variable load that surely acts at the same time as the horizontal force may be counted.
What is the form of the overturning verification?
The design value of the destabilising moment must not exceed that of the stabilising moment – both are taken about the same point.
What are the partial factors for EQU (recommended values)?
all factors 1.0
In EQU the destabilising and the stabilising actions get separate factors; a favourable variable load may not be taken into account.
About which point are the moments taken for a footing on soil, as a first approximation?
about the centroid of the base
about a point at a distance B/10 from the toe
about a point B/3 from the toe
On sound rock about the toe; on soil – because the soil under the toe is pressed in – as a first approximation about a point B/10 from the toe.
What has to be done if e > B/3 (rectangular footing)?
nothing, if the moment check is satisfied
special precautions are needed
the B/10 pivot point must be used
If e > B/3 (for a circular footing e > 0.6·r) the standard requires special precautions – half of the base no longer “works” then.
According to DA-2*, what is the eccentricity calculated from?
from the design values of the actions
from the characteristic values of the actions
from the ground resistance
from the wind load only
In DA-2* the eccentricity is determined from the characteristic actions; the partial factors do not change it.
With one-way eccentricity, at e = B/3, how many times the mean contact pressure is the edge pressure?
infinite
At e = B/3 the compressed length is B/2, the peak of the triangular distribution is 2V/(B/2·L) = 4·V/A – four times the mean.
What are the factors on the permanent actions in UPL?
both 1.0
In UPL the factor on the uplift force is 1.00 and on the self-weight 0.90; on a variable destabilising action 1.50, on a favourable variable one 0.
How is the design value of the uplift force calculated?
with the weight of the structure
from the anchor force
A<sub>k</sub> is the volume submerged below the groundwater level, γ<sub>w</sub> = 10 kN/m³; the uplift force is essentially the resultant of the water pressure acting on the structure.
What is the overall safety against uplift without friction and anchors?
γ<sub>G;dst</sub>/γ<sub>G;stb</sub> = 1.0/0.9 = 1.11 – little, so the water level must be chosen cautiously.
How are the cars parked in an underground car park taken into account?
as a favourable variable load: with 0
as a stabilising permanent load
with a factor of 0.9
with a factor of 1.5
The factor on a favourable variable load in UPL is 0 – the verification must be done for the empty car park.
The 30×15 m box is reached by groundwater 1 m higher. By how much does the uplift force increase?
it does not change
450 m² · 1 m · 10 kN/m³ = 4500 kN – in the example this is +20%.
Which one is NOT a countermeasure against uplift?
extending the base slab
anchoring
temporary flooding
compacting the soil under the base
Compaction helps with settlement, not with the uplift force. The four countermeasures: extension, anchoring, dewatering/drainage, temporary flooding.
When does overall stability have to be checked for a shallow foundation?
near a slope, an excavation, a retaining wall, a bank or a cavity
only for pile foundations
only on rock
never, if the bearing resistance is adequate
According to EN 1997-1 6.5.1: on or near a slope, near an excavation or a retaining wall, near a river, canal, lake, reservoir or the sea shore, and near mine workings or underground structures.
What is the typical failure pattern?
a small wedge under the base breaks out
the soil mass moves together with the footing, the slip surface runs below the footing
the base slides on the foundation level
Overall stability checks the footing and the surrounding soil mass together – the bearing resistance may be adequate while the slope is not.
What are the factors on actions in DA-3?
The load of the footing enters as a geotechnical action, with set A2: 1.0 / 1.3; the shear strength is reduced.
What does the partial factor for friction divide?
the angle φ′ itself
the value of tan φ′
the weight of the slice
the radius of the slip surface
tan φ′<sub>d</sub> = tan φ′<sub>k</sub> / γ<sub>φ</sub> – for example with φ′<sub>k</sub> = 28° and γ = 1.35, φ′<sub>d</sub> ≈ 21.5°.
What usually governs the stability of slopes?
the water conditions
the temperature
the concrete grade of the footing
the wind load
Rainfall, rising groundwater, seepage: the pore water pressure reduces the friction on the slip surface. The loess bank slides in Hungary and the 1972 Hong Kong case were also triggered by water.
The bearing resistance check of the house footing is satisfied. Is overall stability then also certain?
no – the slope may still slide
The bearing resistance checks local failure under the base; overall stability checks the sliding of a larger soil mass. They are two separate verifications.
Which design approach does the Hungarian National Annex prescribe for the bearing resistance and sliding of shallow foundations?
allowable stresses
DA-2*: A1 + M1 + R2. For overall stability DA-3.
What does the asterisk in DA-2* mean?
the partial factors are applied at the end of the calculation, to the effects of actions
a factor of safety of two
it is valid for the undrained state only
the soil parameters are reduced as well
The calculation runs with characteristic values (and so does the eccentricity), the factors come at the end.
In set R2, what is the factor on the sliding resistance of a shallow foundation?
γ<sub>R;h</sub> = 1.1; for bearing resistance γ<sub>R;v</sub> = 1.4.
Which set of factors reduces the strength parameters of the soil?
M2: dividing tan φ′ and c′ (EN recommendation 1.25, for c<sub>u</sub> 1.4).
Which limit state works independently of the design approach, with its own set of factors?
GEO – bearing resistance
GEO – sliding
EQU, UPL and HYD get their own factors.
What replaces the design approaches (DA1–DA3) in the new EC7?
verification cases (VC1–VC4) and MFA / RFA
a single global factor of safety
numerical modelling only
The limit states remain, the assignment of factors changes: verification cases and a material or resistance factor approach.
Which verification case covers static equilibrium and uplift?
VC2: static equilibrium, uplift (the old EQU, UPL).
the resistance is divided by γ<sub>R</sub>
the strength parameters of the soil are reduced by factors
no factors are used at all
a load test is carried out
Material Factor Approach: tan φ′ and c′ reduced by a factor. RFA reduces the resistance (≈ 1.4 for bearing, 1.1 for sliding).
Where does overall stability go in the new suite of standards?
EN 1997-3, Clause 4: slopes, cuttings, embankments
it disappears as a separate check
Clause 4 of EN 1997-3 explicitly covers footings on or near a slope as well.
When must the conflicting first-generation standards be withdrawn?
30 March 2026
30 March 2028
The deadline for national implementation is 30 September 2027, and for withdrawal of the old standards 30 March 2028.
A tall billboard on a small footing, in a storm
Large eccentricity: M<sub>dst;d</sub> ≤ M<sub>stb;d</sub> and e ≤ B/3 are the question.
An empty underground rainwater tank, high groundwater table
The uplift force may overcome the self-weight (UPL).
A cantilever wall with a smooth precast base, high earth pressure
δ = ⅔·φ′<sub>cv</sub> – the friction under the base may be too little.
A family house two metres from the edge of a loess bluff
The slip surface may pass under the house too: overall stability.
A pedestrian underpass near the Danube, during a flood
A long-lasting flood is followed by the groundwater – UPL.
A bridge abutment footing with earth pressure from the backfill, on saturated clay, in the short term
Undrained sliding: R<sub>d</sub> = A<sub>c</sub>·c<sub>u;k</sub>/1.1 ≤ 0.4·V<sub>d</sub>.
A circular shallow foundation of a wind turbine
For a circular footing, special precautions are needed if e > 0.6·r.
Footings of a hall at the edge of a planned deep excavation
Near the excavation the soil mass may slide together with the footings.
The stability of a shallow foundation must be verified for four separate limit states.
Sliding, overturning, uplift and overall stability – each one separately.
Sliding is an EQU limit state.
GEO: it is resisted by the shear strength of the ground.
For sliding, H<sub>d</sub> must also include the active earth pressure transferred to the footing.
H<sub>d</sub> also includes the active earth pressure transferred to the footing.
For a smooth precast footing δ = φ′<sub>cv;k</sub>.
For a smooth precast footing δ = ⅔·φ′<sub>cv;k</sub>.
For drained sliding, the effective cohesion should generally be ignored.
The adhesion depends strongly on the water content and the consistency.
